page.metaTitle: Website Monitoring for E-commerce Brands | WebMonitor.fyi
page.metaDescription: Website monitoring for e-commerce: track competitor pricing, watch for MAP violations, monitor reviews, and catch broken product pages. One platform for the signals that matter.
page.subtitle: Catch competitor pricing changes, MAP violations, review activity, and broken pages from one dashboard built for retail and DTC teams.
page.intro: E-commerce teams juggle a lot of signals at once: competitor pricing, third-party seller activity, customer reviews, supply availability, paid-ad landing-page health. Most teams end up spread across five or six tools to cover it. WebMonitor.fyi runs the monitoring layer in one place. Built for Shopify brands, Amazon sellers, DTC startups, and multi-channel retailers.

challenges.title: Competitor price tracking
challenges.body: When you have 200 SKUs and three competitors, manual price checks are impossible. Pick the hero SKUs where price moves matter most and let monitors with plain-English criteria watch them around the clock — no data team required.

challenges.title: MAP (minimum advertised price) enforcement
challenges.body: For brands selling through third-party resellers, MAP violations show up daily on Amazon and Walmart marketplaces. Daily monitoring catches violations fast enough to enforce.

challenges.title: Inventory and restock visibility
challenges.body: Out-of-stock products on your top retailers cost real revenue. Restock alerts on key SKUs catch lapses before they spread.

challenges.title: Review monitoring across platforms
challenges.body: Amazon reviews, Trustpilot, Google Business — each platform has its own response window. Alerts within your check interval mean responses happen inside the window, not days later.

challenges.title: Launch-day page health
challenges.body: A product launch with a Klaviyo email blast at 9am can pull traffic that exposes any weak point in the checkout funnel. 30-minute content checks (Pro) on the landing and checkout pages catch error banners and broken renders during the launch window.

page.limits: WebMonitor watches the public surface — product pages, pricing pages, public review pages, marketplace listings. Anything behind a seller-only login (Amazon Brand Registry analytics, Shopify admin data, wholesale-portal pricing) needs a dedicated integration. Personalized pricing that varies per logged-in shopper is also outside what a public-page check can see.

faq.q: Can I track my own product across multiple marketplaces?
faq.a: Yes — one monitor per listing per marketplace. Plans include up to five monitors, enough to watch a hero product on Amazon, Walmart, Target, and your own Shopify store side by side.

faq.q: Does this work with private-label or Amazon-exclusive brands?
faq.a: Yes. Public Amazon listings work whether the brand is private-label, branded, or unbranded. For Amazon Brand Registry-specific tooling (which uses an authenticated API), WebMonitor complements rather than replaces it.

faq.q: How do I monitor a product that's currently out of stock?
faq.a: The monitor still polls the page. Set the criterion to "alert me when this product is back in stock" — the alert fires on the first check that finds the page flipped from unavailable to available.

faq.q: Can the customer-success team get a Slack alert on every new negative review?
faq.a: Yes. Set the criterion to "alert me on any review under 4 stars" and route the webhook into a #reviews channel. The team typically responds within hours of the alert.
